Title: Observing Jupiter
Content: Although Galileo Galilei did not invent the telescope, he made significant advancements and refinements to the telescope in `text(1609)`. This refined telescope allowed Galileo to make observations of `text(Earth’s)` `text(Moon)` and the `text(four)` largest moons that orbit `text(Jupiter)`. Presently, spacecraft and space telescopes are used to make more detailed observations of our solar system.
